nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

A message filter that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.

A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and stores first classification data in a persistent store.<SEP>A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.
A model generated by the multi-pass message filter during the first pass, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and purged after use.

An analysis performed on sorted messages that scans mail folders and reads sender information, headers, subject, originating network address, message contents, and attachments to train the multi-pass filter.
A pass using the generated classification model to retrospectively inspect sorted messages and generate a misclassification identification.
A list of sorted messages identified as potentially misclassified, presented to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.

A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform the multi-pass message filtering actions.<SEP>A device configured to receive messages, assign them to message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.

A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.<SEP>A device that executes passes of the multi-pass message filter, stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages.
A memory-resident-only location where the generated classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store, and from which it is purged.
A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and inspected by the multi-pass filter.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.

A recipient associated with the message folders who is presented with misclassification information and enabled to move identified messages to another folder.<SEP>A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder, who may select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.

An address book associated with a recipient that may be analyzed to determine whether a message sender's address is present when generating the classification model.<SEP>A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, whose message sender's address may be analyzed to generate second classification data.
A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, residing exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and deleted upon providing the display of information.
One of a plurality of different folders to which messages are assigned and sorted; a message may be identified as stored in an incorrect message folder and moved to another folder.
A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect folder.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
A memory store at the client device where second classification data resides exclusively.
An interface on the client device through which a user may select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

edges.description: The patent document describes the multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.
The multi-pass message filter generates a classification model during the first pass based on the first pass analysis.
The multi-pass message filter generates its temporary classifier based on results of the previously applied first message filter.
The first pass analysis trains the multi-pass message filter based on which folder each message resides.
The network device's processor is operative to perform the first and second pass actions of the multi-pass message filter.
The multi-pass message filter employs a Naive Bayes classifier.
The first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter occur entirely on the client device.
The processor readable storage medium includes instructions enabling execution of the multi-pass message filter passes.
The first message filter sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders.
The first message filter stores first classification data in a persistent store.
The first message filter is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
The first message filter assigns the plurality of messages to a plurality of different message folders.
The network device assigns messages to message folders using the first message filter.
The second pass uses the generated classification model to inspect the sorted messages.

The generated classification model is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory location.<SEP>The generated classification model is purged from the non-persistent memory location after use.
The classification model is maintained within memory on the user's client device.
The classification model is generated based on analysis including whether a message sender's address is in an address book associated with the recipient.
The first pass scans messages in the user's mail folders and reads sender information, headers, contents, and attachments.
The second pass generates a misclassification identification of sorted messages.
The misclassification identification is displayed to the user so misclassified messages can be moved to a different folder.
The network device is configured to receive a plurality of messages.
The network device communicates the messages over the network to the message folders.
The network device communicates messages over the network to the plurality of different message folders.

The client device executes the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter on the sorted messages.<SEP>The multi-pass message filter is executed on the client device, which runs its first and second passes.
The second classification data is deleted from the client device upon providing the display of information.
The client device identifies messages sorted into an incorrect message folder and provides a display of information so a user can move the message to another folder.
The interface is located on the client device.
The first classification data is stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.
The user is associated with the message folders and can move identified messages between them.
A user is enabled to move an identified message to another message folder.
A user may select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface on the client device.
The second classification data is generated based on an analysis of whether a message sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
The first pass of the multi-pass message filter trains the filter by generating second classification data.
The second pass of the multi-pass message filter uses the second classification data to score each message.
The second classification data is configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device.
The second classification data is generated based on an analysis of a state of a message, a header of a message, or a message content.
The second classification data is generated based on which folder each of the plurality of messages resides.
